summary: Across the fourteen-day window, news items trace an escalating novel coronavirus outbreak originating in China, moving from initial case/death reports to the unprecedented quarantine of Wuhan, extension of the national holiday, rising case counts, and spreading international containment measures including border closures, venue shutdowns, and quarantines of travelers.
mechanism: Escalating reports of a poorly understood, rapidly spreading virus with expanding lockdowns, travel restrictions, and business closures would raise uncertainty about global supply chains, travel, and economic activity, a classic channel for rising volatility in markets pricing macro and sector risk.

claims.claim: China's National Health Commission reported a third coronavirus death and a jump in infections, with spread confirmed to major cities including Beijing and Hong Kong.
North Korea banned foreign tourists and closed its border with China to prevent virus spread.
Chinese authorities placed the entire city of Wuhan under quarantine, halting public transport, as the death toll rose to 17.
Shanghai Disney Resort closed temporarily ahead of Lunar New Year in response to the outbreak.
A leading group led by China's Premier was established to control the outbreak and extended the Spring Festival holiday.
Hubei's Health Commission reported 1,291 new cases and 24 more deaths, bringing the toll to 106.
China's president told the WHO he was confident about defeating the virus, indicating high-level international engagement.
Thousands of cruise ship passengers were barred from disembarking in Italy over coronavirus concerns among Chinese passengers.
By the final day, a planeload of 195 Americans returning from China was placed under quarantine.

competing_explanation: A separate escalation in the Syrian civil war (government forces besieging and capturing Ma'arrat al-Nu'man in Idlib over days 9-12) and the European Parliament's ratification of Brexit on Day 12 are also significant geopolitical developments in the window, though these are more regionally contained or were largely anticipated/scheduled events rather than sudden shocks.
